title: Assemble a mini chopper so it is ready to run, then pulse it once
instruction: Assemble the mini chopper so it is ready to run, then pulse it once. Touch the blade only by its hub. Finish with both arms back where they started.
context: Small kitchen appliances are put together before every use: the blade goes on its pin, and the motor runs only once its top is twisted fully home, which closes its safety switch. The light bowl turns with the motor top unless it is held, so it takes two hands, the kind of everyday job a home-assistance robot would do for someone with weak or painful hands.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. All parts are at real size and mass. (1) The bowl of a cordless electric mini chopper, loose on the table, its middle 25.5 cm forward and 5 cm right of the centre line: clear SAN plastic, 0.14 kg, 9.0 cm across inside and 9.7 cm outside, its rim 7.4 cm above its underside (about 400 ml), standing on a black rubber foot ring; its floor is 0.9 cm up, and a stainless pin 8 mm across rises from the middle to 4.9 cm (a 5 mm tip to 5.3 cm). On its left side a handle: an upright bar 1.8 cm wide and 2.2 cm deep, its middle 9.2 cm from the bowl's axis, from 1.6 to 6.8 cm up, joined to the wall at top and bottom. Just under the rim, on the side away from the arms, a dark dot (the open mark), and 30 degrees anticlockwise from it (seen from above) a dark bar (the lock mark). (2) The S-blade, loose: two stainless blades 1.4 cm wide and 2 mm thick, reaching 4.0 cm from the axis, 6 and 15 mm up a grey plastic hub 2.3 cm across and 4.2 cm tall that is open at the top (the drive socket); 35 g. It stands on its storage post, fixed, 33.5 cm forward and 17.5 cm right: a beech disc 6 cm across and 8 mm thick with an 8 mm peg 4 cm tall. (3) The motor top, loose, standing on the table 19.5 cm forward and 17 cm right: white ABS, 0.28 kg (motor and battery); a plate 10.5 cm across with a collar 1 cm deep underneath that fits round the bowl's rim (9.9 cm inside), a housing 6.8 cm across whose top is 5.6 cm above the plate's underside, a grey PULSE button 3.4 cm across on top, a light beside it (dark), a dark arrow on the plate's edge pointing away from the arms, and on its right side a twist grip: a fin 1.2 cm thick, 2.5 cm tall, reaching 7.6 cm from its axis. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The motor top is caught by the bowl's bayonet once it is set on the rim with its middle within 8 mm of the bowl's axis, tilted at most 8 degrees against the bowl and its arrow within 14 degrees of the open mark. It then stays where it was left until it is turned with 0.3 N m; turned 28.5 degrees anticlockwise from the open mark it clicks home against its stop (locked), its safety switch closes and its light comes on. The blade is on its pin when its hub's axis is within 4 mm of the pin's, the hub's bottom within 4 mm of the bowl's floor, and it is tilted at most 10 degrees. PULSE is pressed when a gripper's fingertip centre is within 1.6 cm (sideways) and 1.6 cm (above) of the button's top for 3 control steps; if the motor top is locked and the blade is on its pin then, the motor runs: the blade spins at 25 rad/s for 1 s. The score is 0.0 once a fingertip (a gripper's fingertip centre or its pads' tips) has come within 1.5 cm of the middle line of either blade's cutting part (the 1.4 cm wide blade beyond 2 cm from the hub's axis), that is, within about 8 mm of its edges. Otherwise 1.0: PULSE pressed while the motor top was locked and the blade on its pin, and at the end the motor top still locked, the blade on its pin, the bowl standing on the table (tilted less than 5 degrees, raised less than 4 mm) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: PULSE pressed that way; 0.5: the motor top locked and the blade on its pin at the end; 0.25: the blade on its pin at the end; else 0.0. Judged at the end of the trial, which ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the bowl, the motor top and the blade still.
reset_notes: Stand the blade back on its storage post, the motor top back on the table where it started (arrow pointing forward), and the empty bowl back in its place with its handle to the left.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz); real-size, real-mass parts. Simplified: the bayonet is a joint that catches the motor top set on at its open mark, holds it where left until twisted with 0.3 N m (a spring for the lugs' friction) and stops at 31.5 degrees; its safety switch counts as closed once home; the drive shaft is drawn only and a pulse spins the blade by setting its speed for 1 s (nothing is chopped); the clear wall is drawn only at rim, foot and seams.
